border noun

also frontier, boundary, border on, borders, bounded by, at the boundary between

classical

Traupman 202
Caes.
Varro

cōnfīnium, cōnfīniī n.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • fīnis, fīnis m. — boundary, frontier; in the plural, territory

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 202, 204

  • terminus, terminī m. — boundary line

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.132: contentiō dē terminīs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 204: frontier

  • attingō, attingere, attigī, attāctum + acc. — border on, adjoin

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. attingō: “to lie near, border upon, be contiguous to”; Traupman 202: border on, attingere; Traupman 281

  • discrīmen, discrīminis n. — dividing line

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 202: at the boundary between Italy and Switzerland, ad discrīmen Ītaliae et Helvētiae

    The classical sense is “that which divides”, hence a distinction or a crisis; Traupman uses it of a boundary line.

Examples

  • Hīc Pȳrēnaeī montēs, in cōnfīniō Hispāniae et Galliae

    Here are the Pyrenees, on the border between Spain and FranceLibellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

  • ab oriente clauditur

    on the east it is bounded byTraupman 282

  • ad discrīmen Italiae et Helvētiae

    at the boundary between Italy and SwitzerlandTraupman 282
